questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: Which type of programming language can a computer's CPU run directly, without any translation?
questions.hint: It's the only one written in pure 1s and 0s.
questions.explanation: Machine code is made of binary instructions (1s and 0s) that the CPU runs directly. All other languages need translating into machine code first.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: Python is an example of which type of programming language?
questions.hint: It uses readable English-like words and is far from hardware.
questions.explanation: Python is a high-level language: its syntax is close to English and far from the CPU, making it easier for humans to read and write.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: Put these languages in order from CLOSEST to the hardware (most low-level) to FURTHEST from the hardware (most high-level).
questions.hint: Machine code is what the CPU actually runs.
questions.explanation: Machine code is closest to hardware (pure binary). Assembly uses short mnemonics for each CPU instruction. High-level languages like Python are furthest from hardware and easiest for humans.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: Why do most programmers write code in high-level languages rather than machine code?
options: High-level code runs faster on the CPU
High-level code is easier for humans to read and write
Machine code does not exist any more
questions.answer: High-level code is easier for humans to read and write
questions.hint: Think about what a wall of 1s and 0s looks like to a person.
questions.explanation: High-level languages use English-like words and are much easier for humans to understand, write, and debug than raw machine code.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: What is the job of a compiler?
options: To run code one line at a time
To translate an entire high-level program into machine code before it runs
To find spelling mistakes in code
To connect a program to the internet
questions.answer: To translate an entire high-level program into machine code before it runs
questions.hint: It does the whole translation in one big batch.
questions.explanation: A compiler translates the whole source program into machine code before it runs. The resulting executable then runs directly on the CPU.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
Computer Systems and Data Science – Oak National Academy

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: What is the main difference between a compiler and an interpreter?
options: A compiler is faster to type than an interpreter
An interpreter translates and runs code one line at a time; a compiler translates the whole program first
An interpreter is only for games
A compiler only works on phones
questions.answer: An interpreter translates and runs code one line at a time; a compiler translates the whole program first
questions.hint: One does it all at once, the other line by line.
questions.explanation: A compiler translates the whole program into machine code before running. An interpreter translates and runs the program line by line as it goes.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
Computer Systems and Data Science – Oak National Academy

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: Python normally uses which type of translator?
questions.hint: Python runs your code line-by-line as you type it.
questions.explanation: Python uses an interpreter, which reads and runs the program one line at a time. This makes it good for quick testing.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
Computer Systems and Data Science – Oak National Academy

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: In computing, what does the abbreviation 'IDE' stand for?
questions.hint: Integrated... Development... E_________?
questions.explanation: IDE stands for Integrated Development Environment — a single program that combines all the tools a programmer needs: editor, translator, debugger, and runner.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: Which of these are tools typically built into an IDE? (Select all that apply.)
questions.hint: An IDE has everything to write, translate, run and fix code — but not data tables.
questions.explanation: IDEs combine an editor, a translator (compiler/interpreter), a runner and a debugger in one place. Spreadsheets are not part of an IDE.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: Which programming construct means running instructions one after another, in the order they are written?
questions.hint: Step 1, then Step 2, then Step 3...
questions.explanation: Sequence is the simplest construct — instructions run in the order they appear in the code, one after another.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: Which programming construct lets a program choose between different paths using IF statements?
questions.hint: It selects which branch to follow based on a condition.
questions.explanation: Selection (IF / ELSE) lets a program choose between different blocks of code based on whether a condition is true or false.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: Which programming construct repeats a block of code (a loop)?
questions.hint: Another word for 'looping' or 'repeating'.
questions.explanation: Iteration means repetition — running the same code multiple times, for example using a FOR loop or WHILE loop.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: A program asks the user for a password and keeps asking until they get it right. Which construct is the main one being used to keep asking?
questions.hint: The 'keeps asking' part is the clue — it's a loop.
questions.explanation: Repeatedly asking until a condition is met is iteration (a WHILE loop). Selection (IF) is used to check the password, but the 'keep asking' part is iteration.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: A game shows a welcome message, asks the player's name, then keeps asking them to guess a number until they get it right. Which constructs does it use? (Select all that apply.)
questions.hint: All three of the main programming constructs are in there.
questions.explanation: Sequence runs the welcome and name steps in order. Selection checks whether each guess is right. Iteration keeps asking until the guess is correct.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: What is a variable in a program?
options: A named container that stores a value which can change
questions.answer: A named container that stores a value which can change
questions.hint: Think of a labelled box that you can put things into and swap out later.
questions.explanation: A variable is a named storage location in memory. The value inside can be read, used, or changed during the program.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt:
After these lines run, what value is stored in the variable score?

score = 10
score = score + 5
questions.hint: Read the second line as 'new score = old score + 5'.
questions.explanation: First score is set to 10. Then score is replaced with 10 + 5 = 15. So score now holds 15.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt:
After these lines run, what value is stored in count?

count = 3
count = count * 2
count = count + 1
questions.hint: Work through each line in order: 3, then double, then add one.
questions.explanation: Start: count = 3. Then count = 3 * 2 = 6. Then count = 6 + 1 = 7.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: Which Python instruction is used to get a value typed in by the user?
questions.hint: The clue is in the name.
questions.explanation: input() pauses the program and waits for the user to type something. It returns the typed text as a string.

further_learning.title: Computer Systems and Data Science – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: Which Python instruction shows a message on the screen?
questions.hint: Despite the name, nothing comes out of a printer.
questions.explanation: print() displays its argument on the screen (in the console). It's the most common way to produce output in Python.

further_learning.title: Computer Systems and Data Science – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt:
Fill in the blank Python instruction so the program asks the user for their name and stores it in a variable called name.

name = ______("What is your name? ")
questions.hint: It's the Python keyword used to get user input.
questions.explanation: input() prompts the user and returns whatever they type, which gets stored in the variable name.

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: What is pseudocode?
options: A real programming language used only by professionals
A way of writing algorithms in plain, structured English that isn't run by a computer
questions.answer: A way of writing algorithms in plain, structured English that isn't run by a computer
questions.hint: 'Pseudo' means 'fake' — it's fake code for humans to read.
questions.explanation: Pseudocode is a structured but human-readable way of describing an algorithm. It doesn't follow strict rules of any one language and isn't run directly.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: Put these pseudocode lines in the correct order to make a program that asks for the user's age and tells them whether they are an adult.
questions.hint: Prompt first, get the input, then decide.
questions.explanation: First we prompt the user, then read their answer, then use selection (IF/ELSE) to decide what to print.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt:
Look at this pseudocode:

INPUT number
IF number > 10 THEN
    OUTPUT 'Big'
ELSE
    OUTPUT 'Small'
ENDIF

What will be displayed if the user enters 7?
questions.hint: Is 7 greater than 10? Follow the ELSE branch.
questions.explanation: 7 is not greater than 10, so the ELSE branch runs and 'Small' is displayed.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: On a flowchart, which shape is used for START and STOP?
questions.hint: It's the only shape with curved ends.
questions.explanation: Ovals (also called terminators) mark the start and end of a flowchart.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: On a flowchart, which shape is used for a PROCESS (an instruction or calculation)?
questions.hint: A plain four-sided box.
questions.explanation: A rectangle represents a process — an action the computer carries out, such as 'set score to 0' or 'add 1 to count'.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: On a flowchart, which shape is used for a DECISION (a yes/no or true/false question)?
questions.hint: It has four points and usually has two arrows leaving it (Yes/No).
questions.explanation: A diamond represents a decision in a flowchart. Two arrows leave it — typically labelled Yes/No or True/False.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: On a flowchart, which shape is usually used for INPUT and OUTPUT?
questions.hint: It's like a rectangle pushed sideways.
questions.explanation: A parallelogram (slanted rectangle) represents input from the user or output to the screen.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize
Computer Systems and Data Science – Oak National Academy

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: Why do flowchart diamonds (decisions) usually have exactly two arrows leaving them?
options: Because they always check for the number 2
Because they ask a yes/no question, so there is one arrow for Yes and one for No
Because they always lead to STOP
questions.answer: Because they ask a yes/no question, so there is one arrow for Yes and one for No
questions.hint: What kind of question gets a Yes or No answer?
questions.explanation: Decisions ask a true/false (yes/no) question, so the flow can go one of two ways depending on the answer.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: You are drawing a flowchart for: 'Ask the user for a number, then display it doubled'. Put the shapes in the order they should appear from top to bottom.
questions.hint: Always start with START, end with STOP. Input first, do the maths, output the answer.
questions.explanation: Every flowchart begins with START and ends with STOP. In between: get input (parallelogram), do the calculation (rectangle), then output the answer (parallelogram).

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: In a flowchart, what does it usually mean if an arrow loops back from a decision diamond to a step earlier in the flowchart?
options: It is showing input being entered twice
It is the end of the program
questions.hint: Repeating earlier steps is exactly what loops do.
questions.explanation: When the flow line goes back to an earlier step, the program repeats those steps — that's iteration shown visually on a flowchart.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt:
Look at this pseudocode:

total = 0
FOR i FROM 1 TO 4
    total = total + i
NEXT i
OUTPUT total

What number is output?
questions.hint: Add together 1 + 2 + 3 + 4.
questions.explanation: The loop adds 1, then 2, then 3, then 4 to total. 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10, which is output at the end.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: A team is writing software that will be sold to customers and must run as fast as possible. Which translation method is generally most suitable?
options: Use an interpreter so customers can edit the source
Use a compiler to produce machine code ahead of time
Write the program in pseudocode and ship that
Send the customers the source code only
questions.answer: Use a compiler to produce machine code ahead of time
questions.hint: Pre-translated machine code runs straight on the CPU with no delay.
questions.explanation: A compiler produces machine code in advance, so the program runs directly on the CPU without translation overhead — usually faster than interpreted code.
